News.title: ISIS bride put make-up on one of her child sex slaves, 5 & 12, before evil husband raped girl as sick couple jailed
News.content:
TWISTED ABUSE ISIS bride put make-up on one of her child sex slaves, 5 & 12, before evil husband raped girl as sick couple jailed

A SICK ISIS couple have been jailed in Germany for keeping two girls as sex slaves.

From the ages of five and 12, the two Yazidi girls suffered a years-long campaign of abuse at the hands of the twisted pair.



The Iraqi couple were sentenced for their horror crimes at Munich today, according to German outlet Bild.

The man, named by prosecutors as Twana H. S, faces a life behind bars while his wife, Asia R.A, was handed a prison term of nine and a half years.



According to the Federal Prosecutor’s Office, the couple were Islamic State members from October 2015 to December 2017.

By late 2015 they had bought a five-year-old girl as a slave and two years later another who was aged 12.

The two children were from the Yazidi religious minority – a group ISIS perpetrated genocide against from 2014 onwards.

Thousands of women and children were kidnapped and enslaved by ISIS throughout the murderous rampage.

According to prosecutors, the girls were forced to do house chores for the couple and were indoctrinated with their terrorist ideology.

Twana allegedly raped both of the girls on numerous occasions.



His wife would apply makeup to the girls and prepare a room for the rapes to take place, the court heard.

When the girls behaved against their captors wishes, they were forced to stand on one leg for extended periods of time as punishment.

Twana beat the elder of the two girls with a wooden broom, while his wife scalded the younger girls hand with boiling water, it is alleged.



In line with ISIS ideology, any practice of Yazidi faith was banned from the house of horrors.

Both girls were forced to dress and abide by Islamic teachings instead.

As ISIS began to loose control of its territory in 2017, the couple fled to Syria.

Here the girls were sold off to another ISIS member, according to prosecutors.

Years later the husband and wife were arrested in Germany.



The woman was accosted by cops in Regensburg, Bavaria and the man was captured in the Roth district.

Charges of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes were filed against both by the Federal Prosecutor’s Office.

Their trial lasted more than a year and a half – as the girls’ nightmare was laid out in front of court.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

One of the girls followed the trial in person and broke down in tears at the sentencing, The Times of Israel reports.

Reading part of her testimony, Judge Philipp Stoll said: “Even dogs were worth more than us. My whole childhood was nothing but suffering.”

News.title: Cowering in shelters & arrested for taking snaps – how Dubai dream became a nightmare for Brit ex-pats
News.content:
FROM glittering skyscrapers to soft sandy beaches, Dubai seemed to have it all.

More than a quarter of a million Brits had made it their home, attracted to the lifestyle, economic perks, and sense of opportunity.



But on the last day of February this year, war broke out over the skies of the Middle Eastern paradise.

After Trump launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, they struck back, targeting allies of the US in the region – including the UAE.



Its image of safety was shattered.

With a lasting peace yet to be secured, BBC Panorama will tonight investigate whether life in the Gulf city state can ever go back to how things were before.

Among the thousands of Brits living in the country when war broke out was Alisha Tyler, originally from Bournemouth.

The 27-year-old moved to Dubai six years ago and worked as a social media manager.

Speaking to Panorama, she recalled the moment she first realised war had broken out.

“It was actually in the morning. I woke up and had a few messages like, ‘Have you seen what’s going on?’” she said.



“I don’t really understand that side of things, going on social media trying to see what’s happening.

“Then I heard a bang and I was like – what was that?”

The city of four million people had long presented itself as a safe haven, separate from the instability that normally plagues the region.

Over the years, it proved to be a remarkable economic success story, though much of that was built off the labour of migrant workers.



Nine in ten of its residents come from overseas, with more than half coming from India.

“Dubai has been phenomenally successful in economics terms,” said Neil Shearing, Chief Economist at Capital Economics.

“It’s become a logistics hub in the Middle East for trade between Asia and Europe.

“It’s developed an enormously successful tourism sector, and liberalised itself and turned itself into a financial services centre.”



It was a haven of peace – until this year.

It was estimated that more than 900 US and Israeli airstrikes hit Iran over a 12 hour period.

Iran soon retaliated, and it had the UAE in its sights.

Brits living in Dubai, like Alisha, now had missiles, drones and debris flying overhead.

Emergency alerts came through on people’s phones, urging them to flee to shelter.



Landmarks like the Burj al Arab hotel and the airport – the busiest airport in the world – were damaged.

“The thoughts running through my head were: I’m a human, I enjoy life, I don’t want to die,” said Alisha.

“When I realised what was going on, I packed a little emergency bag, with passports, water, and me and my housemates filled our car up with petrol in case we needed to drive to the border. “



Mum of two Sabrina, from Kent, had left her job in the public sector to set up a business in Dubai.

“Sunday morning, we were all sitting in the living room and we heard the biggest interception. It shook our windows and doors. And we were like, ‘What is this?’,” she said.

“My older kid would be like ‘What’s that?’, and the younger one would be like, ‘Oh it’s a giant stomping’.

“At night it would wake you up. I was like, why am I here with my kids, I didn’t 

Soon after the strikes started, restrictions were put in place, and air defence systems were put into action.



Almost straight away, 30,000 Brits left and came back to the UK.

On social media, images and videos of the attacks started to go viral.

The sight of burning buildings and terrified tourists running from the beach were a stark contrast to the pristine image normally associated with the city.

But Dubai is not a democracy.

Its rulers clamped down, warning that taking and sharing images was illegal.



Lawyer Radha Stirling is the founder of Detained in Dubai, an organisation which provides assistance to people who are jailed in the city and are in need of help.

She spoke to people who fell foul of this crackdown.

“We had the authorities going specifically to locations, and asking people on the street, can I look at your phone please, and if there happened to be a photograph in there, even if they hadn’t shared it, they were arrested,” she said.



“We estimated that dozens of British citizens had been arrested. They were forced to sign confessions, essentially, to the allegations of cybercrime violations.

“The justification was that it could potentially give away locational details to their enemies.

“But it was more than that. It was more about preserving the reputation of the UAE, to make it appear like it was still a safe place.”

Instead, positive social media posts started circulating.

Many followed a similar formula, praising the UAE’s leaders for keeping them safe.



It appeared to be a coordinated effort to counter the negative press online.

In a statement to Panorama, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said: “Misinformation during times of crisis can have serious consequences, and in some cases, can cost lives.”

They added that 12 British nationals were arrested and that other figures circulating were untrue.



The initial strikes lasted for 39 days, with at least 2274 drones, 29 cruise missiles, and 551 ballistic missiles fired by Iran and its proxies.

“The amount of times I had my family on the phone, going: ‘We need to get you out, we’re sending a plane, you need to come home…’ I’m three daiquiris in. I don’t know what you’re talking about,” said Alisha.

Dubai is still feeling the effects of the war, with tourism most sharply impacted.

Though its airspace has reopened, airline seats in and out of the country are down more than 7 million compared to last year.

The war has the potential to have a negative impact of the same magnitude as the global financial crisis or Covid.



Alisha, in the end, moved back to Bournemouth as the economic downturn led to business drying up.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It did massively slow down. I had to make a decision, that financially, right now I shouldn’t be staying there,” she said.

News.title: Couple among 4 Brits killed in Spanish wildfire are pictured as heartbroken daughter pays tribute & death toll hits 13
News.content:
BLAZE TRAGEDY Couple among 4 Brits killed in Spanish wildfire are pictured as heartbroken daughter pays tribute & death toll hits 13

A BRITISH couple who died after deadly wildfires tore across southern Spain have been identified as their daughter says she is “heartbroken”.

Pete and Fran Gillam were among 13 people who have been killed in the blaze across expat hotspots in Almeria.



Pete and Fran lived in Bedar – a village which was at the epicentre of the fast-spreading fires.

The couple had gone missing on Thursday with the last contact being a text to their daughter Danielle Gillam-Kirton at around 7pm.



Fran had messaged her daughter telling her that she and her husband were evacuating – but then contact cut off and calls failed to go through.

Cops have now confirmed that the pair died in the horror inferno.

Danielle shared the tragic news on Facebook, saying: “We are heartbroken to share that we have received confirmation from the police that Mum and Dad did not survive the fire.

“Thank you for all your love, support and prayers over the past few days. They have meant more to us than we can ever express.”



It comes just days after a British pensioner died in hospital after being rescued from the fires.

The 93-year-old suffered burns on 20 per cent of her body before passing away late on Saturday night – bring the death toll to 13.

Some victims have been so badly burned that not even their gender can be established.



Investigators are now calling on the family members of missing people to provide DNA samples to compare with the scorched bodies.

Pete and Fran Gillam are the first people to have been identified.

Police believe a British woman and her Spanish husband have also been killed, as well as one national each from the US, France and Belgium.

Four bodies found in a burnt-out wreck of a car are also believed to be Brits.

The burnt-out shell of the Honda Accord had a steering wheel on the right-hand side and was discovered on a deadly “trap” route.



The Brits are feared to have died while trying to flee the inferno at Los Gallardos.

They drove down a dry riverbed which turned out to be a deadly “trap”, according to Antonio Sanz, the minister for health and emergencies in the region.

Dry vegetation was the “perfect fuel that, combined with the wind, becomes a ticking time bomb”, added regional president Juanma Moreno.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The wildfires have been some of the worst that Spain has ever seen – with more than 16,000 acres burned to the ground and 1,448 people evacuated.

The Foreign Office said: “Our thoughts are with all those impacted by the devastating wildfires in Spain. We are supporting British nationals affected and their families and remain in close contact with the Spanish authorities.”

News.title: Chilling moment topless Ann Widdecombe suspect takes out bins 3 days after ‘murder’ – as forensics comb for evidence
News.content:
CHILLING new footage has emerged showing a man suspected of killing Ann Widdecombe putting objects in his bins three days after the politician was attacked.

Ms Widdecombe 78, was found dead by a carer at her isolated bungalow in Haytor, Devon, on Thursday morning.



Cops theorised that Ms Widdecombe died some 24 hours before she was found at around midday on Wednesday.

A 28-year-old man was subsequently arrested on suspicion of murder on Saturday evening in Rotherham, South Yorkshire.



Devon & Cornwall Police said they were not looking for anyone else as part of the investigation before counter terror cops took over the probe today.

“New information and evidence” about the death of the ex-Tory minister has come to light, Counter Terrorism Policing South East (CTP) said.



What we know so far…

CTP added the suspect has been re-arrested on suspicion of commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism and “was not known” to the Government’s anti-extremism Prevent programme.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the suspect had no previous links to the scheme designed to identify people at risk of radicalisation.

Video footage from outside the suspect’s home, filmed on Saturday, shows him after he drove nearly 300 miles and allegedly attacked Ms Widdecombe.

It shows the suspect, shirtless, and carrying a bag towards some wheelie bins.



A red Vauxhall Corsa can been seen in the background of the video and appears to be the same car the suspect climbed into before driving to Ms Widdecombe’s property.

The man walks up to the camera with the bag in hand before turning out of the frame to put something in the bins.

He can then be seen doing something off camera, with only his back and arm showing.

He then turns and walks back towards the red car before disappearing from sight.

The video was shot on Saturday, three days after Ms Widdecombe was killed, and shortly before the suspect was taken into custody.



A small dog can also be seen in the video, with a witness saying cops picked up the pooch after arresting the man.



Forensic officers were seen entering a terraced home in Rotherham after the arrest, with a police cordon and several marked vehicles at the scene.

Officers thoroughly checked the man’s bins as they combed through his property.

Clad in white hazmat suits head to toe, the specialist officers can be seen in images peering into the open wheelie bins outside the house where the suspect was arrested.

Several of the forensic specialists can be seen searching in, around and under the bins in images from the scene.

Separate pictures show forensic officers carrying evidence towards their vehicles after searching the area.



Further CCTV seen by The Sun appears to show a young man leaving an address at around 7am on Wednesday morning.

Neighbours told The Telegraph they saw the man putting “some kind of wooden stick” into the passenger side of a red car before driving off.

It is around a four-hour drive from South Yorkshire where the man was arrested to Dartmoor, where Ms Widdecombe lived alone.

Neighbour Courtney Foster said the arrest on Saturday was “really loud”, adding: “They took his dog as well.”

Another resident said: “Loads of unmarked police cars and loads of people ran into house. I feel quite sick to tell you the truth.”



Ms Widdecombe was interviewed on TalkTV at around 8am on Wednesday via video link from her isolated bungalow named Widdecombe’s Rest.

She was then due on Channel 5‘s Matt Allwight show at 1pm – but failed to appear.

In exchanges later made public by ITV News, Ms Widdecombe messaged a staff member at 12.19pm telling them “Received! Panic over!!”

But she did not respond to a Zoom link sent half an hour later at 12.48pm before a producer messaged at 12.55pm asking: “Hi Ann is everything ok?”



Channel 5’s Dan Walker later confirmed her agent was then contacted and asked to go check on her.

It’s understood Ms Widdecombe’s carer found her body in the kitchen on Thursday morning and called 999 for an ambulance, who in turn notified police at 11.40am, nearly a full day after it is theorised she was killed.



Cops later revealed she had sustained severe blunt force trauma wounds after being bludgeoned in the head.

It is believed that her killer was caught on her home CCTV cameras.

On Friday, cops said they believed the attack took place at around 12.30pm on Wednesday – and were working on the assumption she died in a burglary gone wrong.

A 26-year-old man was initially arrested on Friday at an address in Newton Abbot, 11 miles from the scene of the murder.

He was later released from custody, with cops saying he is no longer part of the investigation.



The 28-year-old suspect was then arrested in connection with the investigation on Saturday evening before being re-arrested today by counter-terror cops.

Counter-terrorism officers from North East and South Yorkshire Police assisted with the arrest.

The suspect is described as a white British national.

We previously revealed that Ann Widdecombe’s home was shown on national television just five days before she was killed.

TV channel Quest aired an episode of Celebrity Yorkshire Auction House featuring the late politician on July 2, TV listings show.



In the episode, the inside of Ann’s £600,000 Dartmoor bungalow is shown in extensive detail as she gives host Angus Ashworth a guided tour.

It includes shots of her front door, garden, conservatory, gym, library, kitchen and dining area.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The hour-long season two episode was originally aired in 2022 but was reshown in the 6pm timeslot five days before she was killed at around 12.30pm on July 7.

There is no suggestion that visuals of the home on TV inspired or led to Ann’s killing.

News.title: Short-haul Ryanair trip turns into 12hr flight from hell with ‘drunk’ passenger brawl, mid-air ‘mutiny’ & TWO diversions
News.content:
AIR ORDEAL Short-haul Ryanair trip turns into 12hr flight from hell with ‘drunk’ passenger brawl, mid-air ‘mutiny’ & TWO diversions

A RYANAIR flight, which overran to four times its scheduled length, descended into a nightmare following a drunken brawl, a mid-air “mutiny” and two diversions.

On June 3, a three-hour flight from London Stansted to Albania stretched into a miserable 12-hour ordeal, with infuriated passengers receiving minimal updates.



Flight RK8288 was diverted to Italy and then Greece before finally touching down in the Albanian capital at 5am local time.

Travellers reportedly staged a “mutiny” against the captain after hours of disgruntled confusion.



Trouble began when the plane got caught in a terrifying thunderstorm – ultimately forcing the pilot to perform two diversions.

Passengers were left in the dark until approximately four hours after take-off, when they were told over the speaker that instead of Albania, the flight was approaching an airport in Brindisi, Italy.



The plane was grounded on the tarmac for up to three hours.

Finally the pilot then announced that the plane was ready to take-off again – this time to Tirana, Albania – or so they thought.

Ten minutes before landing, the pilot says they were actually about to land in Thessaloniki in Greece.



A source told the Daily Mail that’s when everyone lost their minds and is when the “mutiny” began.

Anger turned on the pilot, with a group of men aggressively heckling him from outside the cockpit.

They shouted: “He’s a coward, the pilot needs to come out and face us like a man.”

Around a dozen disgruntled tourists demanded to leave the aircraft when it landed in Greece, after the hours of confusion and disappointment.



They shouted: “There’s no way you can keep us here.”

Greek police were eventually called onto the plane, and reportedly told the crew to let the tourists leave.

Following the third take- off, one man threw up on himself just before the aircraft and ran to the toilet – returning moments later, shirtless.

One restless passenger, described as “clearly hammered”, ignored instruction to stay in his seat and began to walk around the plane, leading to an air hostess having to “wrestle him back to his seat.”

The source said: “She literally grabs him, picks him up like a child, and pushes him back down to his seat… it was mental.”



Eventually, the plane managed to land in Tirana at around 5am local time, and the pilot said: “Welcome to Albania.”

Everyone in the aircraft cheered, grateful they had finally arrived at their destination in one piece.

The source said: “We were so dead, so exhausted.”

It is understood that during the flight, the Ryanair crew refused to keep selling food and drink after a certain period.

The source said: “They didn’t give anything out for free, and you couldn’t even buy anything.



“People were understandably thirsty and hungry. We’d already been on the flight for four hours at this point, maybe longer. You couldn’t access anything.”

Travellers were forced to rely on strangers and ration the available snacks between them.

The crew eventually relented and allowed the passengers to purchase refreshments but quickly, all the supplies ran out, apart from a few packs of crisps, the source said.

It is understood the anonymous passenger hasn’t been successful in claiming back any money following the nightmare journey.

When his claim was “automatically rejected”, he chose to escalate his dispute with AviationADR.



In a letter sent to the passenger, seen by the Daily Mail, Ryanair said the flight was “disrupted due to unexpected and extraordinary circumstances, which were beyond our control”.

A Ryanair spokesperson said: “This flight from London Stansted to Tirana (3 June) was diverted to Brindisi due to adverse weather conditions at Tirana Airport, however, subsequently diverted to Thessaloniki Airport due to a thunderstorm.

“After 45 minutes, crew opened the bars on board so that passengers could access snacks and refreshments.

“Passengers booked on this flight received communications via email, SMS and PUSH notifications.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Once weather conditions improved, this flight departed for Tirana at 4:44am local time.”



It comes as a passenger was “sucked up to his shoulders” out of a cabin window after it was smashed open by pieces of the jet’s broken engine.

News.title: Teacher, 25, admits sex with teen, 16, in her truck – and splits from husband who exposed sick crime
News.content:
TWISTED MISS Teacher, 25, admits sex with teen, 16, in her truck – and splits from husband who exposed sick crime

A MARRIED teacher has confessed to having sex with a 16-year-old boy in her truck – and is now divorcing her husband after he exposed her sick crime.

Mackenzie Naught, 25, embarked on a twisted “affair” with a high school student from St John Endicott High School in Washington.



The mum-of-one crept out of her home and had sex with the boy in the early hours of May 3, according to documents seen by The Spokesman-Review.

Almost a week later, she told her husband what she had done – and he promptly reported her to the police.



Cops arrested the disgraced teacher on May 10 and charged with child sex crimes.

She initially denied the vile act – but has now plead guilty in an effort to slash her jail time down from five years to just 12 months.

The sweetheart deal will hold the now-fired teacher “accountable for her actions” while it “spares [the victim] the burden of having to testify at trial” said Whitman County prosecutor Tessa Scholl.

The perv had initially denied having sex with the teen but her husband Garrett then showed police screenshots of her messages with the boy.

The pair had been exchanging “flirty” text messages and the 25-year-old had begged to see the boy, the teen victim told investigators.

Court docs show that the student, after being initially hesitant, finally caved and picked up Naught from her home at around 2:15am.



While her husband slept, the teacher asked the pupil to go to a “little spot” she knew in rural Harwood Hill.

They talked for a while before Naught went in for a kiss and started to “get handsy,” the court filings said.

The two then had sex inside the vehicle and on the truck bed.

The teen then dropped Naught back near her home at around 4am, the boy told cops.



The 16-year-old then also told Garrett about the twisted “affair” on a Snapchat voice call.

Garrett told police he had the boy on the social media app because the couple were friends with his family.

He is also the assistant track coach at the boy’s high school.

Following Naught’s guilty plea to the sordid sex crimes, the couple – who had been married four years – have filed for a divorce.



Naught has also been fired from her job teaching first grade at St. John Elementary School.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The school neighbours the one where her husband taught – and where her victim attended.

She will also be on a sex offenders list for 10 years under the terms of her plea deal.

News.title: Murdered backpacker Peter Falconio’s body could FINALLY be found after 25yrs thanks to new clues, says ex-FBI profiler
News.content:
FOR 25 years, the parents of murdered British backpacker Peter Falconio have been tortured by the fact they do not know where their son’s body is.

Now a former FBI profiler, who has been reinvestigating the case with a team of detectives, believes they may finally have the answer the family have been desperately hoping for.



Peter was 28 years old when he was murdered by John Bradley Murdoch on July 14, 2001, while travelling on a remote stretch of the Stuart Highway, in Australia’s Northern Territory, with his girlfriend Joanne Lees, then 27.

His remains have never been found and his killer refused to tell police where they are before he died.

The investigators say they have identified two “very viable” locations where they believe Peter’s body could lie, after re-examining the movements of his killer alongside advances in behavioural profiling and specialist search techniques.



Former FBI profiler Kathy Canning-Mello told The Sun, ahead of the 25th anniversary of his murder tomorrow: “Peter’s body was never found. It just feels undone.

“Even though we know who the offender was, we still don’t have Peter’s body. So we’re drawn to that as investigators and I think just as human beings, we want to solve this puzzle.

“ I feel very good about these locations. Behaviourally, it just makes sense.”



Murdoch tricked Peter and Joanne into pulling over their Kombi campervan late at night while driving on an isolated stretch through the Outback between Alice Springs and Darwin, during their backpacking holiday through Australia.

Peter got out of the van after Murdoch claimed there were sparks flying from the exhaust, but the killer walked around the back of the vehicle and shot him in the head.

Joanne was then tied up but managed to flee into the bush, escaping what detectives believe had been planned as a sex attack.

Murdoch was found guilty in the NT Supreme Court in 2005 and was serving a life sentence with a non-parole period of 28 years when he died last year.

In an attempt to solve the final mystery of the case, Australian police last year announced a reward of up to A$500,000 (£303,000) for information leading to the discovery of Peter’s remains.



Before he died, Peter’s parents submitted a 10-minute video plea, urging Murdoch to reveal where he had left their son’s body, but he denied any involvement.

Now aged 80, Peter’s mother recently told The Sun: “We’re not getting any younger; I’m 80 this year, my husband is 84 this month, so it was 25 years ago. I was 54 when Peter was killed.”

Kathy Canning-Mello believes the key to finding Peter lies in understanding how Murdoch’s meticulously planned attack unravelled when Joanne fought back.

The team have narrowed their search to two locations, both relatively close to the original crime scene.

“This was absolutely a planned offence. He was prepared, but it was sloppily carried out,” she said.



“After he murdered Peter and grabbed hold of Joanne and she fought back, he had no other recourse.

“He punches her to try to gain control, but he is out of control at this point because this plan has now gone awry.”

She believes Joanne’s escape forced Murdoch to abandon months of planning and improvise instead – a change in behaviour that ultimately points investigators towards where Peter was buried.

“In my experience, talking to child abductors and serial murderers, after they abduct their victim, they are at their sexual peak because they’ve realised this fantasy of abducting their victims,” she said.



“They’re going to take them to a place that’s close so they can be sexually gratified before they murder them.

“Even though he didn’t have Joanne at this point, I think he still had that location in his mind.

“Because he was not thinking clearly, he wasn’t going to come up with another plan. He was going to stick to that original plan of where he was going to take Joanne and Peter’s deceased body.”

One piece of evidence in particular convinced profilers the attack had been planned long before Murdoch struck – a pair of cable-tie handcuffs found in his vehicle.



Kathy said: “He has binding materials, which I think are very instructive in terms of his fantasy behaviour.

“I think this is a crime that he has thought about and fantasised about for a very long time and prepared for.

“The handcuffs really illustrate to me somebody who is, number one, sadistic, but number two, had spent a long time putting these handcuffs together and was well prepared.”

Investigators also believe Murdoch’s previous offending helps explain his actions after Joanne escaped.



“We have several examples of prior offending. The one that comes to mind is when he shot his gun into a group of Aboriginal people because they were blocking the roadway,” Kathy said.

“He got very angry, went home, got his gun and shot into the crowd.

“That was very impulsive, high-risk behaviour. He ended up getting caught and spending some time in prison.

“But that was very instructive to me as to how he behaves when he’s out of control.”



Kathy believes the fact Peter has never been found is unsurprising given the vastness of the Australian Outback.

“In this case, we have the outback, this vast outback, which people would look at and think, ‘Wow, this is like finding a needle in a haystack.’ I think that was one of the comments made early on in the investigation,” she said.

“What is helpful to us as investigators is it hasn’t changed much. Likely wherever he was deposited, his remains are going to be there.”

She said combining behavioural profiling with specialist geoforensic techniques – analysis of the terrain – had dramatically narrowed the search.



“Behaviourally, it just makes sense. Given Bradley Murdoch’s criminal profile, his impulsivity, the fact that this crime went awry, I think the close location would be the most viable and the secondary location based on past behaviour being predictive of future behaviour,” Kathy said.

Plans are now afoot to return to the area for a fresh search in hopes of finding his body within a year.

“I think we have two very viable locations right now,” she said. “It’s just a matter of returning with well-trained dogs to go back to those areas to do a more intensive search.”

The two-part documentary Outback Terror: The Falconio Murder airs on U&W on July 13.

News.title: Entire UK village could be washed away forever after being cut off ‘overnight’ – sparking £20million ‘race against time’
News.content:
A POPULAR coastal village is set to be saved by a multi-million pound grant – but it still faces an “existential” threat.

Several residents have already considered demolishing their storm-battered homes.



Residents of a south Devon village, Torcross, are now in a “race against time” to save their homes, as a number of increasingly severe storms batter the area.

Multiple properties were damaged and a large section of its main road – including part of the A379 coastal road – was washed away last winter after a series of storms hit the village.



Now, the Environment Agency (EA) has agreed to a £19.8m improvement scheme that should “buy the community some time”.

The works, expected to begin taking place this summer, includes re-positioning 55,000 tonnes of rock in front of the existing sea defences, which will create a temporary protective line of rock armour.

The car park storm breach is also set to be repaired by June 2027, along with rock revetment work.

But while residents have experienced “total jubilation” upon hearing news of the funding, fear still remains that the sea defences will not be completed in time.



Hannah Miller, general manager at Start Bay Inn, said it was “a race against time” to get the work done.

She added: “If the storms are anything like they were this year and we don’t have that in place, then it’s going to be a pretty bleak future”.

The repair of the A379 road – known as the Slapton Line – is also not part of the planned Environment Agency project.



This has caused further issues with residents of the 300-strong community, who argue the road is a “lifeline to the village” and its closure has made travel and transport increasingly difficult.

George Arnison, coastal engineer for the EA, said while the scheme was “value for money”, it was not a permanent solution and there were “no easy answers”.

He said: “It will buy the community some time, buy the government some time, buy the Environment Agency some time, to think through what is the long term future here?”

News.title: Ann Widdecombe murder updates: Counter terrorism police leading probe into former MP's death
News.content:
Following "new information and evidence", the Ann Widdecombe murder probe is now being led by Counter Terrorism Policing South East, which says a suspect has been re-arrested

Counter terrorism police are now leading the investigation into the death of Ann Widdecombe, it has been confirmed.

Officers said "new information and evidence has come to light" and so the case is being led by the counter terror team. A 28-year-old white British man was arrested on suspicion of the former MP and MEP's murder, and has since been re-arrested on suspicion of commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

This gives police the powers under the Terrorism Act to detain a suspect without charge for up to 14 days. Devon and Cornwall Police had previously faced a race against the clock to bring charges after the initial arrest.

Counter Terrorism Policing South East gave the update this afternoon, more than four days after Miss Widdecombe's body was discovered at her home in Haytor, Devon.

Head of National Counter Terrorism Policing, Laurence Taylor, said: “Building on the progress made by our colleagues in Devon and Cornwall Police, we now have new information and evidence that means Counter Terrorism Policing is now leading the investigation. We are pursuing multiple lines of enquiry to establish the motivation for this attack.

“Our priority is progressing this investigation quickly, with all the capabilities we have available to us. If anyone has any information, please share it with the police."

News.title: Andy Burnham to be crowned Labour leader after winning support of hundreds of MPs
News.content:
Andy Burnham to be crowned Labour leader after winning support of hundreds of MPs

Andy Burnham, who returned to Parliament last month after nine years as Greater Manchester Mayor, will officially be announced as Labour’s next leader on Friday during a special conference.

View 2 Images Andy Burnham welcomed by Labour MPs last month after his Makerfield by-election victory (Image: Getty Images)

Andy Burnham will be crowned Labour’s next leader later this week after winning the backing of enough MPs to eliminate the possibility of a challenge.

‌



The former Greater Manchester Mayor, who is now certain to succeed Keir Starmer in No10 next week, secured the support of 349 MPs at the close of nominations on Monday evening. This comes after he received an extra 27 nominations today.

‌



It means it is now mathematically impossible for any wannabe rival in the Labour ranks to reach the 81 MP threshold required to throw their hat into the ring.

‌



Mr Burnham, who returned to Parliament last month after nine years as Greater Manchester Mayor, will officially be announced as Labour’s next leader on Friday during a special conference. Around 72 hours later on July 20, the Makerfield MP will walk up Downing Street for the first time as PM.

View 2 Images Mr Burnham will take over from Keir Starmer next week (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

On Monday evening Labour MPs were also set to quiz Mr Burnham on his plans for government during a virtual hustings event organised by the party.

‌



Mr Burnham will tell the Parliamentary party that now is a time to come together - saying his priorities are good growth in every postcode, more power in communities, and putting the cost of living front and centre in the work of the government.

This will provide "breathing space", the PM-in-waiting will say. He is also set to pay tribute to Keir Starmer for delivering on his promise to the Hillsborough families by introducing a Hillsborough Law in his final days in No10.

The Makerfield MP has said he will aim to create a culture where every MP is valued, seen and listened to - an issue that has dogged Mr Starmer. He will tell MPs that now is a "significant moment" for the country - with constituents counting on Labour to come together.

‌



Mr Burnham will also describe the party as a broad church - vowing to reflect this in his appointments. It comes as Keir Starmer kicked off his last week in Downing Street with a diplomatic blitze, joining European allies of Ukraine's wartime leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy for a meeting of the 'coalition of the willing'.

He is also expected to join Bastille Day events in Paris on Tuesday before taking his final Prime Minister's Questions - just over two years on since Labour's landslide election victory.

Earlier this week Rachel Reeves - who is expected to be replaced as Chancellor - warned Mr Burnham that he must remain “last focused” on what he wants to achieve in power.

Article continues below

She told the BBC: “It is important that when Andy walks through that door, that he has a worked-through plan, because governing is hard in Britain, and lots of lots of challenges and shocks will come his way.

“What is really important is that him and his team are really clear about what they want to achieve. As those shocks come along, he needs to stay laser focused on those things that have always motivated him, have always driven him, and are the reason why he wants to lead our great country.”

News.title: British couple killed in Spanish wildfire pictured as heartbroken daughter pays tribute
News.content:
British couple killed in Spanish wildfire pictured as heartbroken daughter pays tribute

Pete and Fran Gillam, who lived in Bédar - one of the villages hit hardest by Spain's wildfires - were among the 13 people killed in the blaze, the couple's daughter said

View 3 Images Pete and Fran Gillam were among 13 people who died (Image: Facebook)

A British couple who died alongside multiple others during the wildfires in Spain have been named and pictured.

‌



Pete and Fran Gillam, who lived in Bédar - one of the hardest hit villages - were among the 13 people killed as deadly fires tore through southern Spain, the couple's daughter said.

‌



The pair had been missing since Thursday evening after Fran sent her daughter a text at around 7pm to say they were evacuating. Contact was then cut off as messages and calls failed to go through to either parent.

‌



Posting to Facebook, Danielle Gillam-Kirton wrote: "We are heartbroken to share that we have received confirmation from the police that Mum and Dad did not survive the fire.

"Thank you for all your love, support and prayers over the past few days. They have meant more to us than we can ever express."

View 3 Images The devastating fire has killed at least 13 people (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Authorities in Spain are now racing to use DNA to identify those who were unable to escape the blaze.

Relatives of those missing have been asked to provide samples to the Bédar's civil office, with many victims suffering burns so severe that it would be impossible to identify them without it.

Officials confirmed that a British couple were among the first victims identified on Monday. A Spanish man and his British wife, as well as a French woman and Belgian man have also been identified as victims.

‌



On Sunday, Andalucían regional authorities said a 93-year-old British woman injured in the fire had died in hospital.

The number of missing people remains unclear until autopsies and the identification of bodies are carried out.

View 3 Images Authorities are carrying out DNA tests to identify victims (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Authorities say burned-out cars which were left abandoned in the road leading out of Bédar were holding passengers that were burned alive as they tried to leave the province.

Bodies found inside a gutted right-hand-drive Honda Accord are likely to be those of at least four more British victims.

Penelope Howe, 54, who lives near Bédar, said her friend's husband died in his car while trying to evacuate with his cats out of the Los Gallardos area of Almería province.

Article continues below

"She's in deep shock," Howe said. "At one point he needed to stop and she spoke to him on the phone. He had got the cats and was trapped in the car. They were speaking together for the last few minutes. That was how it ended."

Scorching temperatures, incredibly dry ground and powerful winds saw the fire spread rapidly across the region on Thursday afternoon.

It comes as much of Europe, including Spain, has battled extreme heatwaves, with some areas of Spain recording temperatures of up to 44C.

News.title: Princess Charlotte's Wimbledon charm bracelet is a £48 bargain with sentimental meaning
News.content:
Princess Charlotte's Wimbledon charm bracelet is a £48 bargain with sentimental meaning

Princess Charlotte was spotted at Wimbledon with a new addition to her jewellery collection – an affordable £48 charm bracelet

View 3 Images Princess Charlotte's Wimbledon charm bracelet is under-£50 and still in stock (Image: Getty)

Made with a gold-tone chain and featuring a mix of charms, glitzy crystals and elegant faux pearls, the Ted Baker buy proved to be the ideal addition to complement Charlotte's custom blue dress. The bracelet's adjustable clasp means it will fit your exact wrist size, which is important if you're buying it for a younger teen.



View 3 Images Princess Charlotte wears a sentinmental charm bracelet for the Wimbledon final (Image: Getty)

View 3 Images Copy Princess Charlotte's look for £48 (Image: Ted Baker)

Charm jewellery has been having a real moment in the fashion world since the start of this year, thanks to trend-driving factors like Belly from The Summer I Turned Pretty's jewellery wardrobe, Dua Lipa's post-honeymoon necklace and Love Island stars wearing their own charm pieces on repeat in the villa.

On Google, 'custom charm necklace' and 'build your own charm necklace' are now breakout trends, while 'chunky charm necklace' and 'locket charms' have both increased by 40% month-on-month, proving that Princess Charlotte has inherited her mum's ability to catch a trend at its peak.
