Sports.title: European champions PSG eye surprise move for France and Aston Villa defender Lucas Digne - as release clause for full-back is revealed
Sports.content:
Lucas Digne is a target for European champions Paris Saint-Germain following his performances for France at the World Cup.

The Aston Villa left-back spent three years PSG from 2013-16 and is seen as an ideal alternative to Nuno Mendes – regarded as one of the world’s top full-backs.

Daily Mail Sport understands there is a clause in Digne’s contract which, if triggered, will allow him to discuss terms with PSG, although it is unclear at this stage what this clause is worth. Villa’s next official fixture is in the UEFA Super Cup against PSG in Salzburg on August 12.

Unai Emery was uncertain about Digne when he took over at Villa in autumn 2022 and quickly brought in Alex Moreno to play in his position.

Since then, Digne has adapted superbly to Emery’s demands, winning the battle with Ian Maatsen to start the biggest games and often winning praise from Emery for his attitude and application.

Daily Mail Sport understands there is a clause in Lucas Digne’s contract which, if triggered, will allow him to discuss terms with PSG

Though Emery would not want to lose Digne, he is 32 and one of the club’s higher earners, having joined for £25million four-and-a-half years ago, when Steven Gerrard was in charge.

Though Maatsen’s form has been inconsistent, he is only 24 and has the potential to become Villa’s regular first-choice at left-back.

Villa did not comment.

Sports.title: Arsenal keeping tabs on PSG winger Bradley Barcola and admire Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers - as Unai Emery's side finalise club-record deal to sign Johan Manzambi after hijacking Newcastle move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Arsenal keeping tabs on PSG winger Bradley Barcola and admire Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers - as Unai Emery's side finalise club-record deal to sign Johan Manzambi after hijacking Newcastle move: WINDOW WATCH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa want Estupinan

As mentioned this morning on Window Watch, AC Milan’s Pervis Estupinan is on Aston Villa’s radar.

The 28-year-old Ecuador international left-back is one of a number of targets being assessed by Villa should Lucas Digne re-join Paris St Germain, as reported by Tom Collomosse.

AC Milan and Ecuador defender Pervis Estupinan is on Aston Villa’s radar this summer

RB Leipzig move for £21m Burnley star

Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is due at RB Leipzig’s training ground later this week for a medical ahead of a £21million transfer.

The 24-year-old centre back has agreed to the move which will be ratified pending his medical.

Highly-rated Esteve has impressed since joining from Montpellier in 2024. His deal will also include add-ons.

Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is due at RB Leipzig’s training ground this week for a medical

Wolves leave £23.4m star out of Portugal training camp

Wolves forward Tolu Arokodare has been left out of their squad for the pre-season training camp in Portugal.

Wolves have rejected loan bids for the player from Fiorentina and Trabzonspor, while a number of other clubs are also interested.

Arokodare cost Wolves £23.4million in September and had a dressing room bust-up with Mateus Mane last season.

Fiorentina are expected to return with an improved bid for Arokodare, who has ruled himself out of a move to Trabzonspor.

Wrexham target Premier League goalkeeper

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has emerged as a target for ambitious Championship side Wrexham.

Club to club talks are underway over a possible deal but there are other teams showing an interest in the 26-year-old.

Patterson is valued around the £7million mark and spent the second half of last season on loan at Wrexham’s promotion rivals Millwall where he made 14 appearances as they narrowly missed out in the play-offs.

Wales star targeted by Sheffield United

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo.

The 25-year-old former Manchester City and Rangers winger is with Brann in Norway but they have told him he is free to leave and he his looking to return to the UK.

Former Leicester star training at Sheffield Wednesday

Former Leicester City winger Wanya Marcal is training with Sheffield Wednesday.

The 23-year-old former Portugal U20 international is a free agent after his contract expired at the Foxes.

Nathaniel Chalobah is also training with Wednesday again after his contract with the club ran out at the end of the season.

Winks set for Italian job

Harry Winks is in Italy completing a medical ahead of his move to Cagliari

Harry Winks is in Rome today ahead of his medical with Cagliari.

The Leicester midfielder is set to sign a two-year contract with the Serie A side.

The 30-year-old former Tottenham star watched Leicester’s 3-0 pre-season win over Northampton on Saturday but was expected to leave after Cagliari agreed terms last week.

Leicester are in throes of adding attacking midfielder Conor Chaplin, formerly of Ipswich, on a free and ex-Southampton goalkeeper Alex McCarthy, also a free.

Santos completes switch

Manchester United have completed the signing of Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £50m.

The agreement is £48m plus £2m in add-ons. Chelsea will also retain a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

Andrey Santos has joined Manchester United from Chelsea

United announced the signing with a video of the Brazil midfielder wearing the the club's shirt and saying: 'Since when I was young, I dreamed of this moment.'

Santos becomes the first signing with Michael Carrick as head coach.

Read the full story here.

Tigers on the prowl in transfer market

Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic has confirmed interest in Croatia internationals Marco Pasalic of Orlando City and HNK Rijeka’s Toni Fruk, plus Hajduk Split’s Rokas Pukštas, a USA Under-23 international.

The three are on an extensive list of targets being worked on by the Premier League new boys who expect to confirm Okan Ozkan as their new sporting director over the next 48 hours.

The Tigers have been in talks with Ozkan, who had been working at Polish club Pogon Szczecin. But the Polish club’s Canadian owner Alex Haditaghi sparked a social media spat with his Hull counterpart Acun Ilicali.

Haditaghi threatened legal action over Hull’s approach for Ozkan, in a succession of messages, whilst copying in the Football Association and Premier League.

Hull still expect to sign Oscar Zambrano from sister club Maribor, and are agreeing a £3m deal to sign Mjallby’s Swedish World Cup left-back Elliot Stroud.

Gunners keeping tabs on Barcola

Arsenal still remain attentive to Bradley Barcola’s situation at Paris Saint-Germain.

They also admire Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers and accept both will be expensive to prise away.

Arsenal remain attentive to the situation of Paris Saint-Germain and France winger Bradley Barcola

Liverpool also admire Barcola. He is one of a number of wide attackers being assessed by the club but they are yet to make a formal enquiry.

Arsenal are awaiting Leandro Trossard’s decision over his proposed move to Besiktas.

The Gunners have a deal lined up for Christos Tzolis from Bruges which they may accelerate when Trossard leaves.

Another player that is on Arsenal’s radar but lower down their list is Norway’s Antonio Nusa.

The RB Leipzig winger had a decent World Cup on the back of making 35 appearances in the Bundesliga last season but there have been concerns about his knee condition since a move from Bruges to Brentford collapsed on medical grounds in 2024. A specialist later cleared him to play and he joined Leipzig.

Meanwhile, midfielder Christian Norgaard is attracting interest from Saudi club Al Jazira.

Dobbin closes on Southampton move

Aston Villa forward Lewis Dobbin is closing on a £9million move to Southampton.

The 23-year-old scored 10 goals on loan at Preston last season and was also wanted by Wolves, Middlesbrough and Sheffield United. Villa will receive further add-ons based on performances and appearances.

Villa forward Lewis Dobbin is closing in on a move to Southampton

Villa, who are finalising a club-record deal for Freiburg midfielder Johan Manzambi, have also been offered the chance to sign Pervis Estupinan from AC Milan.

The 28-year-old left back previously played for Watford, Brighton and Villarreal.

Sports.title: What I learned from Andoni Iraola's note-perfect Liverpool unveiling: How he'll avoid traps Arne Slot fell into, his hint on club's transfer plans and why I was blown away by new Reds boss, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
AI is taking over at Anfield and, funnily enough, Andoni Iraola’s first official engagement as Liverpool boss felt like artificial intelligence had really arrived.

Not because he was robotic in his body-language and words, as some managers are. Anything but. Instead, it was because everything he said was note perfect, as if he had been programmed to only give inspiring, well-informed and measured responses.

It is easy to fall into the trap of falling for every word a new boss says, of course. The first press conference is always a chance for some easy wins: say a few buzzwords and the supporters will be salivating, especially this fanbase which has been eager for change.

Former Bournemouth boss Iraola knows that as much as anyone and recognises that his words mean diddly squat if they aren’t backed up with results on the pitch. Yet, as far as opening addresses go, the Basque nailed it.

Daily Mail Sport was in the room and has picked out some of the biggest talking points from the man tasked with turning around Liverpool’s fortunes after a dismal campaign cost Arne Slot his job...

Andoni Iraola was officially unveiled as Liverpool's new manager today - and everything he said was note perfect

The Basque boss gave well-informed and measured responses that will have been music to Liverpool fans' ears

Words to fill fans with confidence

It won’t make the same headlines as Jose Mourinho declaring himself ‘The Special One’ or even Jurgen Klopp insisting that he wanted to turn Liverpool ‘from doubters into believers’ but Iraola’s first words will be worth looking back on next spring.

‘I would like to give them (the fans) a team they can feel proud of,’ he said when asked about his objectives. ‘I think football and especially Liverpool is about connecting.

‘Connecting with the people, connecting with our supporters. I've been on the other side at Anfield. I’ve experienced the goal that (Federico) Chiesa scored on the first day of the season (against Bournemouth last year).

‘You can feel the stadium, I would love to have this every time we play but that has to come from us, inside the pitch. We have to be a team that works hard, intensely, aggressively, vertically so everyone can be identified and everyone can feel comfortable supporting this team.’

Last season, Liverpool fans – even the most hardened Slot backers – could not feel too much pride watching a team with a weak defence and uninspiring attack.

Even when they won matches, they were hardly thrilling displays that got bums off seats, while Anfield became less a fortress and more a place where teams would rock up and fancy their chances – the Reds won just 10 of 19 home games, compared to 14 the year before.

Iraola wants to change that and intends to do so with a high-octane style of play, though the 10 home draws he managed at Bournemouth might not go down too well here if that were replicated.

Iraola wants to get Liverpool fans excited with a high-octane style of play, having experienced a raucous Anfield atmosphere on previous trips with Bournemouth

'We have to be a team that works hard, intensely, aggressively, vertically so everyone can be identified and feel comfortable supporting us'

Righting the wrongs of Slot

For 12 months, Slot could have walked into any bar in Liverpool and received a free pint (not that he would, as he kept a low profile). He was a hero and fans loved him after he brought them some of the best days of their lives with the Premier League title win of 2024-25.

For the next year, though, he was better off keeping his head down. From hero to zero in the eyes of many. By the end, pretty much everything the Dutchman said and did was criticised, some of it justifiably and some of it unfairly.

Whenever a manager has been sacked, the new guy can achieve some small wins. ‘Manager X reverses ban on ketchup,’ is the usual headline, soon to be followed a year later by ‘Manager Y bans ketchup at the training ground’.

But Iraola said some things in this press conference that suggested he will do things very, very differently to Slot.

For example, the Basque insisted he wanted to get a true feel for the city of Liverpool, immersing himself in the culture and taking some pictures.

He said: ‘I would also like to go to the city, experience the city: I know some places, I would have to take some pictures. But it's also part of the magic of being the Liverpool manager and I would like not to change too much.’

See you in PopWorld on Friday night then, Andoni? Maybe not, but this approach delighted fans after Slot decided to live in Cheshire, away from the hubbub of Liverpool.

It may seem an unreasonable stick to beat a manager with, added to the fact Slot was criticised for spending lots of his days off with family back in the Netherlands, but it is something the supporters care about.

Iraola's first press conference suggested he will avoid the excuses that caused his predecessor Arne Slot (left) to come under fire from fans

Not here to make excuses

Another thing Slot was criticised for was how, in the eyes of outsiders, he would be full of excuses. He would often complain about injuries, referees and how his team struggled to convert chances into goals against stubborn defences.

Iraola, though, insisted: ‘I prefer to face low blocks. We’ll be in control of the game, we’ll concede less chances and spend a lot of time in the opposition half. Those are the scenarios we have to face.’

Instead of complaining, the new boss says he is looking forward to working out how to unlock teams who come to defend.

Relaxed, personable demeanour

You need not be a body-language expert to read Iraola’s mood on Monday morning: grinning like a Cheshire cat, plenty of toothy smiles, polite hand-shakes, eye-contact, trying to answer all questions rather than side-stepping them (that might not last!) and all done in a relaxed manner.

He came across as a likeable individual and that can only be a positive thing for all concerned, be it staff or players.

Iraola was also prompt and took his seat at exactly 11am, not a minute early and not a minute late. It’ll keep the broadcasters happy at least.

Ready to give youth – and Harvey Elliott – a chance

Several first-team players were at Liverpool's HQ on Monday, including new defensive signing Jeremy Jacquet, Iraola’s ex-Bournemouth charge Milos Kerkez and a few youngsters looking to impress the new boss.

Harvey Elliott has already been back for a week, having trained with the Under 21s, and he will be given a chance to prove himself this pre-season.

Iraola said Harvey Elliott (pictured) will get a chance to impress in pre-season following his disappointing loan to Aston Villa

His former Bournemouth player Milos Kerkez (pictured) will be another out to impress on tour in the US

The 23-year-old signed for Aston Villa last summer on a loan deal that would become permanent when he made 10 appearances. It was seen as a foregone conclusion he would be staying at Villa Park for good but it never came to fruition as it was clear Unai Emery did not fancy him.

Now Elliott is back and Iraola said: ‘I’ve seen him with this eagerness to show himself, to get himself ready again. He will have a chance during the pre-season, we will need him.

‘Harvey, last season had to be very difficult for him, because it was a strange situation where basically they couldn’t even put him in to play.

‘I think he uses what he has experienced, the bad situation, to make him even more eager to be a Liverpool player.’

Youngsters will also be given chances to impress under Iraola this pre-season, with the squad to travel to Chicago next Monday. The Reds play three friendlies, with the tour also taking in Nashville and New York.

Calmed fans over quiet transfer window

Liverpool fans are an anxious bunch at the best of times, always hungry for news updates. The fact this summer has been rather quiet in terms of transfer rumblings has sent some poor souls into overdrive.

Iraola calmed fears that they might be going to go into the season undercooked, though, by saying: ‘We've signed two players (Jacquet and winger Victor Munoz). We need more, we know this.

‘We are working on this. As a coach I want the players here from day one, selfishly, but we know it doesn't work like this, we're working hard for those signings.’

Iraola impressed in his first briefing. Now it is time for the higher-ups to provide him with a competitive squad with a few fresh faces. Next stop Chicago.

Sports.title: 'I'm sorry': Sacked former England Test coach Brendon McCullum breaks his silence over his dismissal
Sports.content:
Brendon McCullum has apologised to England fans for the failure of the Test side to win any of the four series against Australia and India during his four years in charge.

England lost 4–1 away and drew 2–2 at home against both teams, and McCullum said: ‘Fundamentally, we just weren’t quite able to win those two marquee series. We weren’t able to get the results in those, and for that I guess I can only say sorry.’

McCullum also confirmed he had been sacked, rather than choosing to step down. ‘I got a tap on the shoulder, and obviously I am disappointed,’ he said.

‘But at the same time, I fully respect the decision. We’re in a results business, and our results weren’t good enough. It’s time for someone else to have a go.’

Brendon McCullum was sacked as England Test coach on Sunday - but remains in charge of the white-ball teams

He denied that his philosophy had been about ‘playing recklessly’, and insisted: ‘My method is about trying to build an environment where people are able to be the best versions of themselves, so they can handle the pressure moments when they’re at their highest. We didn’t always get it right, and I accept that.’

McCullum’s immediate task is to rebuild the one-day team’s fortunes, starting tomorrow/today with the first of three 50-over matches against India at Edgbaston.

‘I’ve got the enthusiasm for it,’ he said. ‘With the World Cup not too far away, we’ve got an opportunity to get ourselves in a position where we’re a realistic chance of lifting the trophy.’

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola issues update on Harvey Elliott's future after Liverpool midfielder's 'very difficult' loan spell at Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola issues update on Harvey Elliott's future after Liverpool midfielder's 'very difficult' loan spell at Aston Villa

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is ready to welcome Harvey Elliott back into the fold after a 'difficult' season away from Anfield.

Elliott spent last season out on loan to Aston Villa under manager Unai Emery but only managed to bank 109 minutes of action.

And speaking in his first press conference since taking the reins from Arne Slot this summer, Iraola was full of praise for the 23-year-old’s work ethic.

Iraola said: ‘Harvey is here with us, I have seen him with the eagerness to show up, get super ready, he’ll have a chance in pre-season, we’ll need him and it’s a good sign.

‘I hope we can see him in a good place. I think Harvey comes from last season. [It] had to be difficult for him; strange situation. They couldn’t even play him, and I think he uses this experience - the bad situation - to make himself even more eager to be a Liverpool player.’

An obligation to buy clause built into the loan agreement with Aston Villa meant they would be forced to buy Elliott for £35 million once he reached a certain number of appearances for the team.

Harvey Elliott only managed 109 minutes of action for Aston Villa during his loan spell last season

He is now back with Liverpool hoping to prove he can be a part of Andoni Iraola's side

To avoid the financial hit, Emery kept Elliott on the bench for the second half of the season.

Speaking to reporters in May, the Villa manager apologised for the ‘embarrassing’ situation that cost Elliott a year of development in a key stage of his career.

Emery said: ‘My apologies for Harvey Elliott, is every day in my mind. But it is [about] responsibility. We have our responsibility and Liverpool have their responsibility.

‘Of course, it is something embarrassing for everyone involved. As a human and as a person, how the season has gone has been difficult.’

Elliott has an opportunity to get back on track with Iraola’s arrival as the Spanish manager looks to sign more players and boost the squad in the absence of top players such as Hugo Ekitike and Mohamed Salah.

Two signings have already been made, with Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz joining Liverpool.

Sports.title: England vs Argentina 'value' tickets rocket up to £287,000 as fans fume at FIFA 'exploitation'
Sports.content:
England vs Argentina 'value' tickets rocket up to £287,000 as fans fume at FIFA 'exploitation'

England take on Argentina in the World Cup semi-final on Wednesday but ticketless matchgoing fans face extortionate prices due to resellers

View 2 Images England fans face paying eye-watering prices for a ticket to Wednesday's World Cup semi-final against Argentina (Image: World Cup 2026 News Pool (WCNP))

England and Argentina supporters face paying at least $2,700 (£2,000) for a ticket for their World Cup semi-final, with FIFA accused of exploiting supporters. The Three Lions have their sights on ending the reigning champions' hopes of successfully defending their crown on Wednesday and booking a place in their first World Cup final since 1966.

‌



However, fans are facing extortionate ticket prices to get a seat to watch Harry Kane battle it out with Argentine great Lionel Messi. England supporters' ticket account, England_Tic on X, says the governing body are exploiting supporters as they shared a screenshot of ticket prices up to an astonishing $287,500 (£214,927) for a 'supporter value' tier seat.

‌



The seats are listed on FIFA's official ticket resale website. The tickets are split into products and categories with category one, the highest-priced, being seats closest to the pitch to category four, which is deemed the most affordable and positioned in the upper tier.

‌

Lionel Messi ready to defy doubters again as Argentina great gives England verdict READ MORE :

However, even category four has prices ranging from $3,105 (£2,321) to $40,250 (£30,000) for resold tickets. The account posted: "And here we are.... the big games.

"Once in a lifetime. Bucket list stuff. The games where FIFA can exploit 'the beautiful game' and it's passionate fanbases. On FIFA;s market place $60 'supporters value tier' tickets are being listed from $3,737.50.

‌



"The 15% fee charged by FIFA to both buyer and seller would come to $1,121 on the cheapest ticket. FIFA don't want supporters to attend they want them to sell their tickets. #greed."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

England booked their place in Wednesday's semi-final thanks to Jude Bellingham's double as Thomas Tuchel's side came from behind to beat Norway. The Real Madrid midfielder equalised in the second-half, cancelling out Andreas Schjelderup's first-half opener.

‌



Defending champions Argentina await in the last-four after beating Switzerland, also after extra-time. Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister rose highest to open the scoring against the Europeans but they charged back and equalised through Nottingham Forest's Dan Ndoye.

The tie was tipped on its head while Switzerland were in the ascendancy, when Breel Embolo was sent off for a second bookable offence. The striker became the first player to be dismissed after the video assistant referee utilised the new mistaken identity rule. Embolo, who had already been booked, was adjudged to have dived following a challenge from Leandro Paredes as he was initially booked.

View 2 Images England defeated Norway in the quarter-finals courtesy of a Jude Bellingham brace (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez scored the crucial goals in the tie in extra-time to secure their place against England. They will play the winners' of either France and Spain as Les Bleus look to avenge their defeat from four years ago, while Luis de la Fuente's side are looking to replicate their European Championships success.

Ahead of Wednesday's semi-final, police are on red alert at the Mercedes-Benz Arena in Atlanta due to limited segregation at the stadium. Officers have been made aware of the historical context behind England and Argentina with both having history on and off the pitch, stretching from the war over the Falkland Islands and Diego Maradona's infamous Hand of God goal 40 years ago.

Sports.title: The mentality monsters semi-final: How England can finally kill off Argentina's World Cup defence
Sports.content:
England have reached the point where every mistake carries the weight of history, and few international rivalries carry more history than the one that awaits the Three Lions on Wednesday (July 15) in Atlanta Stadium.

Standing between Thomas Tuchel's side and a first World Cup final since 1966 is an Argentina team that have survived rather than stormed through a tournament in which they are chasing their own piece of immortality - winning back-to-back World Cups for the first time in their history.

Both sides have ploughed on through the knockouts but rarely looked convincing while doing it - and that's what makes this semi-final so intriguing.

Each boasts an attacking talisman in Harry Kane and Lionel Messi still capable of putting up elite numbers in the twilight of their international careers. Both teams also possess a younger attacking player growing in importance, in Jude Bellingham and Julian Alvarez, who carry their nation's hopes forward.

‌



View 6 Images Argentina's defender Cristian Romero celebrates after the quarter-final over Switzerland

Both teams, above all, have scored their way through defensive problems rather than solved them, creating the prospect of the most open game of the tournament.

Speaking on ITV's post-match coverage of Argentina's 3-2 comeback win over Egypt, Gary Neville summed it up perfectly. "You watch [Cristian] Romero and [Lisandro] Martinez, and they're the best 'worst centre-halves' in the world," Neville said.

"You watch them, they give goals away constantly. But they don't care about giving goals away because they'll score goals at the other end. They have massive personalities and they keep going."

‌



In short, anything could happen.

Delving into both sides' performances with Machine Football, it's easy to see why England v Argentina is being billed as a game of the tournament contender - and why England must be ready to seize their moment.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Argentina have won games without control

Across six matches, Lionel Scaloni's side have scored three goals on five occasions and been involved in two of the three 'games of the tournament', 3-2 against Cape Verde and 3-2 against Egypt. They have also conceded six goals, but from 3.4 expected goals against. Only Spain (1.8) have accumulated a lower 'xG against' rating from the four teams remaining in the tournament.

They are, therefore, allowing relatively few high-quality chances, primarily as a result of their dominance of the ball - no side has completed more accurate passes per match than Argentina's 611.5 - but individual lapses continue to punish them.

Their defensive duel numbers reveal the extent of the problem. Against Algeria they won just 31% of defensive duels. Against Austria that dropped to 17%. Jordan, 11%. Egypt, 24%. Cape Verde, 26%. Switzerland, 27%.

In none of their six matches have Argentina won even a third of their defensive duels. Despite their typical grip on possession, the Albiceleste are not consistently controlling opponents - they are simply finding ways to outscore them.

‌



England's tournament has followed a surprisingly similar pattern. Tuchel's side conceded two goals against Mexico despite progressing, needed extra time to overcome Norway and have looked vulnerable whenever opponents attack quickly in transition.

Both teams arrive in Atlanta with attacking momentum, but neither arrive with defensive certainty.

England player ratings as 9/10 Jude Bellingham rescues Three Lions AGAIN READ MORE :

Left-sided vulnerability

View 6 Images Argentina's Lisandro Martinez after Egypt scored a second goal - later disallowed - in their round of 16 match (Image: Getty Images)

The clearest weakness sits on the left side of Argentina's defence.

‌



Lisandro Martinez remains one of the world's best ball-playing centre-backs, and has historically made up for his relatively diminutive 5'9" build with strong anticipation, but Machine Football's model understandably places him in the 4th-lowest percentile globally for aerial duels.

Alongside him on the flank, Nicolas Tagliafico wins defensive duels more reliably than 86% of other full-backs, yet ranks high, in the 97th percentile, for fouls committed and just the 9th percentile when defending dribblers one-versus-one.

That combination creates an obvious route for England. Harry Kane has already shown how dangerous he is when quality deliveries reach the penalty area, thumping home Declan Rice's corner against Croatia in England's World Cup opener nearly a month ago.

Whether from Rice, Bukayo Saka, Anthony Gordon or England's other set-piece routines, crosses targeted towards Martínez's zone could prove to be one of England's most productive attacking weapons.

‌



On the opposite flank, right-back Nahuel Molina presents a different opportunity. His attacking qualities are readily apparent, ranking in the 77th percentile for accelerations, but defensively he wins duels at only a 42nd-percentile level and ranks in the 22nd percentile aerially.

If England can isolate either Argentine full-back one-v-one, there is space to exploit.

England must be cautious against transitions

The reason this fixture feels so open is that England carry many of the same concerns.

‌



John Stones - who acquitted himself well against Erling Haaland in the Norway quarter-final - profiles as a strong aerial defender and ranks in the 95th percentile for defensive headers globally, but sits in only the 31st percentile for tackling.

That matters against the speed of Julian Alvarez and the wizardry of Lionel Messi. Machine Football's model ranks Messi in the 100th percentile for dribbling - the best bar none - plus the 99th percentile for shot quality and 99th percentile for combination play. Just don't let him take another penalty, if you're an Argentina fan.

View 6 Images Messi's attacking contributions have remained consistent into his late 30s and his World Cup performances have silenced any doubts that he can still perform at the highest level (Image: Machine Football)

Needless to say, Messi is unlikely to hurt England aerially. He will, however, hurt them between the lines if he is allowed the space to do so.

‌



Along with his mesmerising dribbling ability, the great man has accumulated more expected assists than anyone else at the tournament (3.4). England's centre-backs have looked considerably stronger defending crosses than they are likely to look with Messi running directly at them.

Despite scoring a tournament-high four set piece goals and having an impressive 33.3% crossing success rate to their name, Argentina are just 15th for accurate crosses per match (4.3), way behind England in third (6.0).

The Albiceleste are also 31st in the tournament for accurate long balls per match (18.3), making plain their preference for creating chances through clever passes centrally, rather than going direct.

England will need to remain switched on at the back to avoid being opened up by a moment of Messi magic.

‌



A potentially defining midfield battle

Despite their quality on the ball, Argentina's midfield is hardly impenetrable. Enzo Fernandez has played every minute of the knockout stage but has won only 25 of his 60 duels across the tournament — a success rate of just 42%.

Opponents have also dribbled past him five times from eight attempts. Given he is typically deployed alongside Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister, whose often-sluggish performances in the Premier League last season drew plenty of criticism, it would be fair to say Argentina's midfield may struggle to defend in open spaces if England's central players can attack with energy and purpose.

View 6 Images Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez plays a deep role for Argentina but lacks the defensive steel to keep their midfield watertight against transitions (Image: Machine Football)

Argentina's midfield four against Switzerland - Fernandez, Mac Allister, Rodrigo De Paul and Leandro Paredes - have averaged 4.5 sprints per 90 each across the World Cup.

‌



England's midfield trio of Jude Bellingham, Elliot Anderson and Rice have averaged 6.0 each, underlining the greater intensity the Three Lions can call upon.

Those numbers suggest Bellingham, or even potential substitutes Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze can attack Argentina centrally rather than simply working around them.

If England eliminate Fernández from the first phase of transition, Argentina's back four has already shown it can become exposed - and that presents the perfect opportunity for England's player of the tournament so far.

How Jude Bellingham went from being disrespected by Thomas Tuchel to England's World Cup hero READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel is getting best out of Jude Bellingham - but England tension is growing issue READ MORE :

The World Cup's most open game?

Neither side has consistently controlled matches. Top scorers Argentina (17 goals) have nevertheless struggled to contain their opponents and have had to make the fourth-highest tackles per game (20.2) of any team in the tournament, exposing their reliance on last-ditch interventions.

‌



England, meanwhile, have conceded two goals in one game twice already, and goalkeeper Jordan Pickford has the third-worst goals prevented figure (-2.7) out of the 44 goalkeepers to have made an appearance at this year's World Cup.

View 6 Images Jordan Pickford had a wobbly game against Norway (Image: AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

Both teams, however, possess enough attacking quality to punish those weaknesses.

Kane attacking Martinez in the air. Messi drifting into the spaces in front of England's defence. Bellingham slaloming through a ropey Argentina midfield. Saka isolating Tagliafico.

‌



The individual match-ups all point in the same direction: if either goalkeeper keeps a clean sheet, it will go against almost everything both teams have shown throughout this World Cup.

Outscoring Leo Messi, who has already bagged eight and shows no sign of slowing down, sounds like a tall order and - if we're all honest - it will be.

But Kane, Bellingham and the rest certainly have the tools and will feel they have the momentum to seize the day, finally putting an end to Argentina's stubborn World Cup defence.

Sports.title: Pubs forecast to sell nearly 10 MILLION extra pints for England's World Cup semi clash with Argentina
Sports.content:
Pubs forecast to sell nearly 10 MILLION extra pints for England's World Cup semi clash with Argentina

Up to 26 million fans are expected to tune in to watch England's semi-final battle with Argentina - with the 8pm kick-off forecast to deliver a bonanza for pubs

View 4 Images England fans are expected to fuel a surge in sales for pubs, bars and supermarkets (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Hopeful England fans are forecast to guzzle up to 10 million extra pints for Wednesday’s World Cup semi-final clash with Argentina.

‌



After the heroic win over Mexico, and the nail-biting quarter final against Norway, a nervy nation is preparing for Thomas Tuchel and the team’s biggest game yet of the tournament. With football fever is sweeping the nation, as many 26.2 million are expected to tune in for England’s high-stakes semi-final clash against Argentina, according to latest predictions from discount website VoucherCodes.

‌



Many are expected to flock - as they have for previous games - to pubs, bars and fan zones to share the drama with friends, family and strangers alike, with some bursting at the seams.

‌



View 4 Images Some pubs have been fully booked for the World Cup, delivering a much needed boost to trade (Image: provided)

World Cup LIVE: FIFA face backlash as Kane weighs in on Tuchel vs Bellingham row READ MORE :

Lionel Messi ready to defy doubters again as Argentina great gives England verdict READ MORE :

VoucherCodes estimates seven million - a record for the tournament - will roar on the Three Lions in hospitality venues, with fans forecast to drink 9.7million pints. The surge will boost hospitality sales by £60.5million from drinks alone with an additional £37.8million going on food.

Trade body the British Beer and Pub Association has produced its own estimates and reckons pubs alone could serve an extra six million pints for the game. The average Wednesday in July would see pubs sell around eight million pint so, if its estimates are right, it would equate to a massive 75% surge in sales.

‌



View 4 Images Pubs, shops and fans alike will be hoping England can overcome the might of Argentina and Lionel Messi (Image: JAMES COOK/EPA/Shutterstock)

Emma McClarkin, BBPA chief executive, said: “Thanks to the World Cup, we’ve seen millions of extra pints sold off the back of home nations matches. Given the nail-biting stakes, we expect Wednesday to be the most successful night of the tournament, with more than six million extra pints potentially sold – which is a bigger boost than we’d normally see on a Bank Holiday or New Year’s Eve.

“The Three Lions have not only delivered on the pitch, they’ve brought fans and communities together, boosted pubs up and down the country, and created some unforgettable memories. Now all they need to do is bring it home!”

‌



View 4 Images Jude Bellingham's heroics against Norway triggered wild celebrations in pubs at the final whistle (Image: AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

England’s 2-1 win over Norway - led by Jude Bellingham ’s inspiring performance - drove a 23% increase in spending in pubs and bars according to payment provider Dojo. It reported a 152% spike ahead of extra time in the match, while transactions also jumped after the final whistle, as the nation let out a sigh of relief and ordered an extra drink to celebrate.

With Wednesday’s game kicking off at a prime time 8pm - England’s earliest yet in the tournament - an estimated 19.2 million people are also expected to watch the game at home or with friends. Supermarkets and others shops will be the big winners with a £357million spending spree, VoucherCodes estimates.

Article continues below

The bulk of sales will come from food and drink (£238m), sportswear (£44m) and electrical items (£25m). Clair Hughes, savings expert at VoucherCodes, said: “We’re now at that nail-biting point where England might actually win the World Cup.

"With every win and a step closer to victory, the excitement is growing and fans are becoming increasingly more lenient with their wallets. Football fever has people spending more than ever to enjoy the biggest sporting event of the summer.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel has performed England World Cup masterstroke with help from FA boffins
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has performed England World Cup masterstroke with help from FA boffins

England have reached the semi-finals in Thomas Tuchel's first tournament in charge with the German coach's decisions on his squad now looking like masterstrokes ahead of the clash with Argentina

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has proven spot on when it comes to his World Cup squad (Image: Getty Images)

When Thomas Tuchel picked his World Cup squad, there was a magic number in his mind. The Football Association had done the research, Tuchel had looked at previous tournaments and the sums appear to be adding up.

‌



England boss Tuchel told his coaching staff that history suggests that 21 players of the 26 man squad will get game time at a World Cup. That includes two reserve keepers but therefore means that only three outfield players are likely not to get even a kick at the tournament.

‌



So far, Kobbie Mainoo, Ivan Toney and Trevor Chalobah are the only players not to have seen any action in England’s six games at this World Cup. Reserve keepers Dean Henderson and James Trafford have not got off the bench either.

‌



And yet, here we are, over a month into the tournament and it is obvious that England’s substitutes have been crucial in playing their part in the campaign.

Manchester United fans have become increasingly frustrated and vocal because Mainoo has not had a look-in despite his impressive Euro 2024 and renaissance at Old Trafford under Michael Carrick.

FIFA proven right on England vs Norway spidercam row as new evidence emerges READ MORE :

Toney spoke about being an important player for the group while Tuchel also admitted that he picked the striker to be on “special operations” as he is a penalty specialist and supersub. He has yet to do either.

‌



Chalobah was a late replacement after Tino Livramento and you get the feeling he is happy to be along for the ride after breaking into his summer holiday in New York to join the squad. But the reality is the rest have made a real difference. And they will be just as important from here on in.

Dan Burn has come into his own in the last two games as he starred against Mexico as ten-man England manned the barricades to keep out their opponents. The Newcastle defender did the same against Norway. Djed Spence struggles from the start but has been sensational from the bench, he was magnificent against Norway.

Ollie Watkins might have been seen as first reserve to Harry Kane but he has had just six minutes against Panama while his Aston Villa teammate Morgan Rogers has been a revelation. While Rogers has not started, he has made an impact whenever he has come on and has linked brilliantly with Jude Bellingham.

‌



View 3 Images Morgan Rogers has impressed in his role as a super-sub (Image: Getty Images)

Bukayo Saka was excellent from the bench against Norway while Eberechi Eze was also a half time substitute in that game, slotting into central midfield after Declan Rice went off injured.

It was Tuchel who first started talking about using “finishers” and he was referring to his options on the wing because whether it was Saka, Noni Madueke, Marcus Rashford or Anthony Gordon who started, the other two would come on.

‌



But actually it has been the same story on other parts of the pitch because of the heat, the conditions and the climate. It is energy-sapping.

The figure of 21, according to those with a knowledge of the research, was based on previous tournaments, the likelihood of challenging climate and also the extra game in an expanded 48 team tournament.

Tuchel knew he would have to lean on his squad and utilise players like never before. It is impossible to guess where the team will finish - but the hope was always they would go a long way.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has led England to the semi finals of the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Now they find themselves at the semi-final stage. Disillusioned players who are fed-up at not getting game-time are a distraction and can be negative on the rest of the group.

But Toney talked about wanting to be part of it. Chalobah was happy for the experience. You suspect that Mainoo wanted more action. Maybe that is to come.

‌



However, it also bears out Tuchel’s idea that not only would he have to pick the right players but also the right characters because if it turns out that only 21 will get a slice of the action then the rest have to be invested.

Just over a week ago, everyone suspected Burn was just along for the ride. And yet now he has become a bit of adult figure and a key player from the bench.

That justifies his selection and there is still time for others to become heroes with the possibility of extra time epics, penalties and two huge games in five days.

Sports.title: Who White House are hoping wins 2026 World Cup ahead of Donald Trump trophy lift
Sports.content:
Who White House are hoping wins 2026 World Cup ahead of Donald Trump trophy lift

Andrew Giuliani, head of the White House's World Cup task force, has revealed who he wants to win the trophy this summer as four teams remain in the tournament

View 2 Images Donald Trump's advisor has spoken out over his World Cup hopes (Image: Win McNamee, Getty Images)

White House adviser Andrew Giuliani has declared he wants England to win the World Cup this summer. Andrew Giuliani, Donald Trump's executive director of the White House Task Force on the FIFA World Cup 2026, said it would be a 'beautiful victory' for the Three Lions to lift the trophy in less than seven days time.

‌



Thomas Tuchel's side need to defeat Argentina to confirm their place in the tournament's finale, where either France or Spain will await them. Jude Bellingham guided England into the semi-finals in a tense victory over Norway.

‌



And with the United States knocked out, the White House official has been required to find another team to get behind for the remainder of the tournament. Giuliani is giving his backing to England despite being fully aware of the heartbreak they have faced over the last 60 years.

‌



But the 40-year-old is convinced of England's credentials. "You know, if the United States can't win on our 250th birthday, then a great storyline would be the English coming to America and winning during our anniversary celebrations," Giuliani told the Daily Mail.

"'It's been 60 years of hurt, I gather, for England, so that would be a beautiful victory for them if they won the tournament. I do absolutely think England can go all the way, they are one of the top teams left now."

FIFA proven right on England vs Norway spidercam row as new evidence emerges READ MORE :

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Giuliani went on to credit Harry Kane and Bellingham as the driving forces behind England's shot at glory. The US advisor called upon former Chelsea boss Tuchel to instill belief into his side.

"Harry Kane is the number one goal scorer for the England team, and if they are going to win the tournament, he will be the main reason. He is one of the main players on the team, and he and Jude Bellingham are fine athletes.

"England strike me as being an exceedingly well-balanced team you have to be confident and what the coach has to drill into them is that they have the potential to win. "

‌



View 2 Images Andrew Giuliani wants England to win (Image: KENT NISHIMURA, AFP via Getty Images)

It has also come to light that Kane is a firm favourite of US President Trump, who is set to be involved in the trophy lift on Sunday. Trump described the Bayern Munich striker as a "great player" and a "great guy" on social media.

The England skipper hit the golf course with Trump back in 2024 in Florida, with Kane recently revealing that the President had extended an invitation for a round during his visit to Palm Beach.

‌



"I played all right to be honest, but 18 months ago he invited me to play when I was down in Palm Beach," said Kane. "So, when the president invites you somewhere, it was a pretty surreal experience just to meet him and obviously play golf with him."

Kane continued: "His golf is pretty good to be honest with you. I hope I can play golf as good as him when I'm his age, that's for sure. A unique experience, but I was just grateful that he invited me to play."

Sports.title: Brendon McCullum reveals 'tap on shoulder' as he breaks silence on England Test axe
Sports.content:
Brendon McCullum reveals 'tap on shoulder' as he breaks silence on England Test axe

Brendon McCullum saw his time as England test head coach come to an end last week after three years in the role and he has now spoken out on the decision for the first time

View 2 Images Brendon McCullum was sacked last week (Image: Getty Images)

Brendon McCullum has revealed he got a ‘tap on the shoulder’ before his England Test sacking last week. McCullum, 44, had been in charge of the red-ball side since 2022 but the ECB confirmed that he had ‘stood down’ in a statement.

‌



McCullum’s exit came after a dismal run of seven defeats in nine matches, with England having suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat in the Ashes over the winter in that time.

‌



Speaking about the decision to move him on, McCullum has confirmed that he was given a nudge before being pushed. He said: “Yeah, I got a tap on the shoulder.

‌



“I was disappointed but at the same time I fully respect the decision. We’re in a results business and fundamentally our results weren’t good enough. It’s time for someone else to have a go.

“We didn’t always get it right. For that, I put my hand up and say we weren’t able to get there.”

Brendon McCullum sacked as England Test coach as future of white-ball job decided READ MORE :

And while McCullum was disappointed to lose his role, he further suggested that England’s recent form was a reason why he has been moved on.

‌



He added: “We just weren’t quite able to win those big series, against India and Australia, the two marquee series. We just weren’t able to get the results and for that I guess I can only say sorry.

“I was the leader of that group. I was in charge of the team culturally, in charge of the team tactically, in charge of the team results-wise as well.

View 2 Images Brendon McCullum will still be in charge of England's white-ball side (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“If you don’t get the results, being a results business, fundamentally you get replaced. I’m not unaccustomed to that, I’ve been around this game for 20-odd years and I know if you aren’t getting the results, someone else needs an opportunity. I put my hand up for that and accept it wasn’t good enough.”

McCullum will still be involved with England by staying on as the side’s white-ball coach. On the split coaching set-up, the New Zealander said: “Once the new coach comes into play we will sit down and unpick a lot of this stuff.

“You’ve got different staff, players, schedules are different, obviously captaincy discussions, but it’s about what is right for English cricket. I’m sure that will be a collaborative process. I also wish the new Test coach all the best.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi ready to defy doubters again as Argentina great gives England verdict
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi ready to defy doubters again as Argentina great gives England verdict

Lionel Messi is under no illusion of the test that awaits Argentina when they play England with the World Cup winner readying for face the Three Lions for the first time

View 3 Images England stand between Lionel Messi and a third World Cup final (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

Lionel Messi has described England as a “powerhouse" - now, finally, the GOAT will go toe-to-toe with England in Wednesday’s semi-final with Atlanta.

‌



It is remarkable the player - regarded by most as the Greatest Of All Time - has never played against England before. And now Messi is eyeing another piece of history against one of Argentina’s greatest football rivals. This is a grudge match which will go beyond the pitch as the reigning world champions face Thomas Tuchel’s Three Lions.

‌



Messi, 39, appears to be on a one-man mission to help Argentina win back-to-back World Cups for the first time since Brazil in 1962. Four years ago in Qatar, we thought it would be Messi’s farewell as he helped Argentina overcome France on penalties after arguably the greatest final of all time.

‌



And yet here is Messi lighting up this World Cup with goals, assists and more brilliance which surely sets him apart from any player in history.

Messi is currently tied with Kylian Mbappe on eight goals in the battle for this World Cup’s Golden Boot. Mbappe is currently ahead courtesy of the assist tie-breaker after providing three which is one more than Messi.

Argentina granted permission to wear black armbands after FIFA reject France request READ MORE :

Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have six goals each and this tournament is shaping up to be the battle of the titans. For the first time ever, FIFA’s top four teams have also made the semi finals because the tennis-style draw which has kept them apart until now.

‌



Pundits were queuing up four years ago to say this Argentina side is a long way from being their best. But they still defied expectations to go and win it. The same accusation is levelled at Argentina this time and yet Messi’s magic means elevates the team to a different level.

They are never beaten. Even with the clock ticking down as they trailed 2-0 against Egypt in the last 16, Messi gave Argentina hope and a never-say-die spirit.

Messi’s very presence on the pitch gives them an aura and a fear factor which overwhelms opponents. Egypt crumbled and Argentina went through. He is a long way from being the dynamic winger who would tear English teams apart in the Champions League.

‌



View 3 Images The Argentine, now 39, remains hugely influential (Image: Elsa/Getty Images)

Incredibly, former Barcelona and Paris Saint Germain star Messi scored 27 goals and provided six assists in 36 appearances against English opponents in the Champions League.

These days, the Inter Miami star tends to play through the middle, he has become a moments player who comes to life at the right time rather than dominate games for 90 minutes. But when Argentina were losing to Egypt, Messi did what he knows best: he shifted out to the right wing, cut inside and worked his magic. Suddenly Messi was transformed into his old self because he is chasing a dream.

‌



Another World Cup. The Argentina fans are singing about Messi, the Falklands (Malvinas) and putting a fourth star on the shirt. When the Argentina players sing in the dressing room, they have adopted the chant.

The song is translated to: “I am a supporter of the national team. I cheer it on with all my heart. We won the third title with Lionel, and we want to be champions once again.

"And 32 years later, La Scaloneta will avenge, the trophy that was taken from the No 10, the one we were not allowed to lift. I want to see the fourth star shining on the jersey. I am Argentine from cradle to grave, for the Malvinas, for Diego, for Leo’s final chapter. Argentina, I want to see you become back-to-back champions.”

‌



View 3 Images Lionel Messi is seeking to win successive World Cups (Image: Getty Images)

That dream of winning back-to-back World Cups is driving Messi and Argentina on. The rivalry with England gives them even greater motivation.

As does the memory of Diego Maradona. When Messi was interviewed after the quarter final win over Switzerland, he not only described England as a “powerhouse” but also as a “special opponent” as he brought up 1986.

‌



England have an impressive record against Argentina - only two defeats, although they did lose on penalties in 1998 - but have not played them since a friendly in November 2005 which explains why Messi has never faced them.

But Messi’s World Cup is all about breaking records, writing new chapters of history and chasing even more glory to put his status as the greatest of all time beyond any doubt.

Sports.title: Real Madrid 'reject £21m bid' for ex-Man Utd star as Xabi Alonso requests Chelsea transfer
Sports.content:
Real Madrid 'reject £21m bid' for ex-Man Utd star as Xabi Alonso requests Chelsea transfer

Xabi Alonso is eyeing reinforcements at Chelsea are is keen to reunite with Alvaro Carreras, whom he worked with last year when the pair were at Real Madrid

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is looking to add to his Chelsea squad (Image: Fadel SENNA / AFP via Getty Images)

Chelsea have seen a £21million bid for Real Madrid left-back Alvaro Carreras knocked back with Xabi Alonso hoping to lure him back to England with the promise of more minutes.

‌



The Blues are in the market for a new left-back following the exit of Marc Cucurella, who left to join Los Blancos. Carreras only moved to the Bernabeu last year after impressing at Benfica, where he was finally given the chance to show his quality.

‌



There he worked with Alonso before his dismissal, but the Spaniard is keen to reunite with a player who was once on Manchester United's books, but never given an opportunity.

‌



Spanish outlet Sport say Alonso has requested that Chelsea sign Carreras as he believes he is the ideal replacement for Cucurella, but their offer for the 23-year-old was immediately rejected by Madrid.

Real reportedly want at least £43m to sanction his exit despite Carreras by no means being a regular - and Alonso will hope to use the incentive of more minutes to convince him to join Chelsea.

Xabi Alonso drops Alejandro Garnacho bombshell after confirming Enzo Fernandez transfer stance READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso tells players his clear non-negotiable in first Chelsea interview READ MORE :

Netherlands international Jorrel Hato, who joined Chelsea last summer for £36m, can play at left-back but the Blues are hoping to bring in more cover in that area. Chelsea's approach in the transfer market has been widely criticised since BlueCo took charge of the club - with a number of players failing to deliver.

‌



Alonso has been appointed and looks to have been handed more control than any Blues boss in recent memory. His exploits with Bayer Leverkusen, where he won the double, have marked him out as a top manager and the ex-Liverpool star has spoken about his desire to change their playing style and ultimately get back in Europe.

View 2 Images Alvaro Carreras has impressed at Real Madrid (Image: Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Alonso said: "To be part of that process, how we want to play, how we want to approach a game, that's my goal. That's what I am looking forward to having the whole squad. Early days, I am happy, but, for sure, I want to be there (in Europe). To be at Chelsea you need that ambition and hunger."

Article continues below

He then doubled down on that, insisting the players must have that drive. "We need hunger, passion, we need to want to improve," added the Spaniard. "The Premier League is so competitive. We need to prepare ourselves, we need to be determined in the details, how they want to play. But the most important bit is our game."
